title: Decide guardrails gating policy: required-by optimization type/tier/model family + phased enforcement
creator: Aditya Rao
description:
Policy decision needed for Optimize Guardrails: when to require evaluation gating before applying Optimize-driven config changes.

Background
Optimize can propose cost-saving changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles, routing tweaks). These changes can materially impact output quality and/or formatting. We are introducing a mandatory quality gate at the control-plane when an optimization is applied (UI + API).

This ticket locks:
1) The matrix of when gating is required (optimization type x customer tier x model family / provenance)
2) Rollout stages and enforcement behavior (observe-only -> soft-block -> hard-block)
3) Override availability and auditing requirements
4) Safe-degrade behavior when eval runner is unavailable (block vs manual approval)

Inputs / relevant docs
- PRD: Optimize Quality Guardrails Gating (Confluence): optimize-quality-guardrails-gating-prd
- UX spec: optimize-apply-flow-gating-ux-spec
- ADRs:
  - adr-optimize-gating-enforcement-point
  - adr-threshold-schema-and-versioning
- Applied ML: guardrails-metric-taxonomy-and-thresholds
- Quant-specific policy: quantization-guardrails-policy
- SRE: guardrails-rollout-checklist, safe-degrade guidance

Definitions
- "Gating required": Apply is blocked until eval suite completes and thresholds pass.
- "Observe-only": Run evals + store results + show in UI, but do not block apply.
- "Soft-block": Block apply by default; eligible users can override with justification (audited), subject to rate limits.
- "Hard-block": No override in-product; exceptions only via internal admin / break-glass + post-hoc review.

Policy dimensions
A) Optimization type
- Quantization profile change (e.g., FP16 -> INT8, INT8 -> INT4)
- Batching changes (max_batch_size, continuous batching params)
- Caching changes (prefix/KV cache enablement + size policies)
- Routing tweaks (fallback policies, region routing, cost-based routing)

B) Customer tier / deployment
- Hosted API (self-serve)
- Dedicated capacity (SLA, isolated pools)
- Private (VPC/on-prem): regulated workloads, stricter change control

C) Model provenance / family
- Redwood-catalog models (Redwood-verified)
- Customer-pinned model versions (still catalog, but pinned)
- Customer-supplied models (Private/on-prem) where support exists but benchmarks vary

Decision (approved)

1) Default gating requirement matrix (GA target)

1.1 Quantization
- Hosted API: Gating REQUIRED for any quantization profile change.
- Dedicated: Gating REQUIRED.
- Private: Gating REQUIRED.
Rationale: Highest risk of subtle quality drift (formatting, reasoning, instruction-following), and historically highest customer escalation rate.

Additional quantization constraints (enforced via policy):
- Block unsafe transitions by model family (e.g., certain families disallow INT4 for long-context / tool-calling workloads until explicitly certified).
- Mandatory suite list includes: tool-calling / structured-output sentinel suite (if route uses tools/JSON), plus baseline task-success + safety checks.

1.2 Batching
- Hosted API:
  - If change affects token ordering/streaming semantics, or if route is tagged tool-calling / structured output: Gating REQUIRED.
  - Otherwise: Gating REQUIRED for tier >= "Growth" plans; Observe-only for free/trial (see rollout).
- Dedicated: Gating REQUIRED.
- Private: Gating REQUIRED.
Rationale: Batching can affect decoding/streaming edge cases and output formatting (esp. with function calling / JSON mode). Also batching changes are frequently applied for cost reasons.

1.3 Caching
- Hosted API:
  - If route uses tool-calling / structured output OR has "strict_format" tag: Gating REQUIRED.
  - Otherwise: Observe-only initially; move to REQUIRED after pilot validates low false-positive rate.
- Dedicated: Gating REQUIRED.
- Private: Gating REQUIRED.
Rationale: Prefix caching is usually quality-neutral but can surface correctness issues (stale prefixes, prompt boundary bugs) and can amplify formatting drift for strict outputs. We want gating for strict routes immediately; broader enforcement after we validate harness coverage.

1.4 Routing tweaks
- Hosted API:
  - If routing change can result in model variant substitution (fallback to compatible variant) or cross-region routing: Gating REQUIRED.
  - Purely cost-based routing within same model+version+region: Observe-only (telemetry + canary), then revisit.
- Dedicated:
  - If fallback enables variant substitution: Gating REQUIRED.
  - Otherwise: Observe-only.
- Private:
  - If routing can change model identity or quantization variant: Gating REQUIRED.
  - Otherwise: Observe-only.
Rationale: Routing changes are broad in scope but not always quality-affecting. We gate when the change can alter model identity/behavior.

2) Enforcement phases (rollout plan)

Stage 0: Internal only (1-2 weeks)
- Observe-only for all optimization types.
- Goal: Validate eval-runner latency, caching effectiveness, artifact links, and audit events.

Stage 1: Pilot (3-4 weeks)
- Quantization: Soft-block (override allowed for restricted roles) for pilot tenants.
- Batching: Soft-block for pilot tenants on tool-calling/structured routes.
- Caching/Routing: Observe-only except strict routes.

Stage 2: GA initial
- Quantization: Hard-block for all tiers (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), with override only for Enterprise break-glass (see Overrides).
- Batching: Soft-block -> Hard-block over 2 weeks, starting with Dedicated + Private, then Hosted Growth+.
- Caching: Soft-block for strict routes; observe-only elsewhere.
- Routing: Soft-block only when model identity/variant substitution is enabled.

Stage 3: Expanded enforcement (post-GA, follow-up)
- Caching: move broad caching changes to Soft-block once prompt-set coverage targets met.
- Routing: evaluate expanding beyond model-identity changes depending on incidents / customer feedback.

3) Overrides (who/when/how)

Principle: Overrides exist to prevent long customer outages / contractual breaches, not to bypass quality checks as a matter of convenience.

3.1 Eligibility
- Hosted: No self-serve overrides. (Support can initiate internal process; customer does not click through.)
- Dedicated: Overrides allowed only for approved customer roles (Enterprise Admin) AND Redwood internal oncall, during soft-block stage.
- Private: Overrides allowed only for approved customer roles AND Redwood internal oncall, during soft-block stage.
- Hard-block stage: customer-facing override disabled. Break-glass requires Redwood internal admin action + post-hoc review.

3.2 Requirements
- Mandatory justification text (min length, no PII policy reminder).
- Optional second-approver requirement for Private customers (configurable per tenant; default ON for Private).
- Rate limit: max 2 overrides / tenant / 7 days (configurable) to prevent policy circumvention.
- Audit logging must include: initiator, approver (if any), policy version, suite versions, prompt-set revision, metrics, pass/fail reasons, and override flag.

4) Safe-degrade behavior (eval runner down / timeout)

Default behavior by tier:
- Hosted: BLOCK apply when gating required and runner is unavailable (fail-closed).
- Dedicated: BLOCK apply by default; allow manual approval workflow for approved tenants during pilot only.
- Private: Manual approval required (do not allow automated apply without gating). If runner unavailable, UI should present "manual approval required" state rather than ambiguous timeout.

Timeout standard:
- Target: 15 min p95 for gating runs (suite-dependent).
- Apply flow: show progress states; after 20 min, mark as "Timed out" and do not apply.
- Retry: customer can re-run; system should de-dup identical runs via caching.

Success criteria for policy
- Prevent regressions: 0 P0 customer incidents attributable to Optimize-applied quantization/batching changes without gating.
- Override rate: <5% of gated applies within first 30 days of GA (excluding pilot), and trending down.
- False positives: keep <10% of gating failures overturned after rerun + investigation.

Open questions / follow-ups (tracked as separate tickets)
- Should we require gating for caching changes on all routes once prompt-set coverage reaches target? (Follow-up after Phase 2 pilot metrics.)
- How to handle customer-supplied models in Private where baseline prompt sets are missing? (Likely require customer-provided prompt sets for hard-block stage; need DevEx docs + Support playbook.)
- Contractual SLAs: ensure policy language consistent with enterprise commitments and change-management expectations.

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket)
- Matrix above agreed by Product (Aditya), Applied ML (Jonas/Selene/Sana), Platform (Ethan/Jordan), SRE (Sean/Rafael), and Security reviewer (Naomi/Kevin).
- Rollout stages and override eligibility documented and referenced in PRD.
- Linear dependencies aligned so engineering tickets implement the decided policy (schema flags, enforcement stages, RBAC).

Decision log
- 2025-01-22: Proposed default gate-all for quant + batching; caching/routing conditional. (Initial draft.)
- 2025-01-29: Applied ML requested hard-block for quantization at GA; SRE requested fail-closed for Hosted. (Incorporated.)
- 2025-02-04: Exec sponsor (Priya) approved override constraints and second-approver default for Private.
- 2025-02-06: Final signoff captured; mark Done.
comments: 2025-01-16 (Jonas Weber): +1 gating required for quantization across the board. We should not allow "INT8->INT4" without a mandatory tool/JSON sentinel suite for any tool routes; we’ve seen formatting drift even when aggregate task-success stays flat.

2025-01-17 (Ethan Park): From control-plane perspective, easiest if policy engine can express: required_suites_by_optimization_type + conditional based on route tags (tool_calling, strict_format) and tier. Please avoid a policy matrix that requires runtime introspection we don’t have at apply-time.

2025-01-21 (Sean Gallagher): For runner-down scenarios, Hosted should fail-closed. For Dedicated/Private we can consider a manual approval state, but we need to be extremely explicit in UI and audit logs. Also, rate-limit overrides; otherwise this becomes the default path during incidents.

2025-01-24 (Selene Huang): Agree on staged enforcement for caching. Coverage is not there yet for non-strict chat routes; enforce immediately for tool-calling/structured outputs and keep rest observe-only until we close prompt gaps.

2025-01-29 (Naomi Feldman): Override must require justification + audit event fields sufficient for SIEM export (who/what/when/why). For Private customers, default second approver is appropriate; make it tenant-configurable but default ON.

2025-02-04 (Priya Natarajan): Approving policy with the constraint that customer-facing override is disabled once we move to hard-block. Break-glass must be Redwood-admin only with post-incident review.

2025-02-06 (Aditya Rao): Final policy captured in description and referenced in PRD. Moving ticket to Done; engineering will implement via ENG-3913 (enforcement) + ENG-3920 (override path) + ENG-3926 (release plan).
